toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
This looks like one chance QC flag, not a faulty analyzer or a bad reagent lot. The failed Level 2 result passed on repeat. The other two levels and sodium and chloride were fine. Level 2 averages are unchanged since the lot change. 43 patient samples re-run on Analyzer A agreed with Analyzer B within 0.10 mmol/L. The patient median is steady. All 182 scheduled QC runs were done on time, so the short-staffing theory isn't supported. About one chance flag a month is expected at this QC volume. I can't say whether a sampling glitch or plain chance caused it, so don't record a cause as confirmed.

Ward 6's high potassiums are split evenly between Analyzer A and Analyzer B. They coincide with the tube outage, which delays samples, and with four renal overflow patients. Both are plausible explanations, but neither is proven.

What to sign off: return Analyzer B to potassium service and close the review of the 186 results with no amendments. Optionally add extra Level 2 QC for a week. Don't widen the limits. Don't recall about 2,900 results or quarantine the lot. Ask Ward 6 to send repeat samples, and get the tube repaired.
